title: NovaForge integrator + pilot framing
summary: Introductory partner discovery with NovaForge to map reseller/integrator model, pilot scope for private VPC onramp, and technical compatibility checks (GPU images, network, KMS). Agreed to an initial 6-week pilot focused on a small customer use-case; Redwood to deliver benchmark runbook and security docs. Follow-ups: share pilot SOW template, provide perf baseline spreadsheet, schedule infra deep-dive next week.
topics: GPU image compatibility and runtime optimizations
action_items: Maya Chen | send pilot SOW template and standard reseller addendum | 2025-09-16
Owen Brooks | share lightweight benchmark runbook + perf spreadsheet (token/sec, p99 latency) | 2025-09-18
Samir Patel | provide NovaForge baseline infra spec and preferred GPU images (OS + drivers) | 2025-09-14
Jules Navarro | draft commercial handshake options: referral vs reseller margins | 2025-09-20
next_steps: Schedule infra deep-dive (hosted by NovaForge infra) next Tue 9/16 10am PT
Run initial compatibility checklist on a small VM pool and share results
Redwood to open pilot project in CRM and link SOW
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-09-11 15:00 PT · Duration 1:02 · Attendees: Maya, Owen, Jules (Redwood); Evan, Priya, Samir, Lina (NovaForge)

00:00 - Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, super excited to kick this off quickly-ish, um, we can do quick intros and then jump into how you'd like to partner.
00:18 - Evan Cole: yep thanks maya, im evan cole, i run cloud partnerships at NovaForge, we're an integrator/reseller for hybrid cloud infra, focus on telco and regulated customers mostly.
00:30 - Priya Menon: priya here, cto. We're evaluating partners for an onramp to GPU inference customers, a mix of hosted and private installs.
00:45 - Maya Chen: great, super helpful. Quick intro from our side, I'm maya, AE, owen is our SE who'll lead the tech side; jules will handle partner ops and contracts.
01:02 - Owen Brooks: hey all, quick technical note, at Redwood we run a unified runtime across hosted, dedicated, and private modes — continuous batching, kv cache, kernel selection — so integration points tend to be: network/VPC peering, container images or AMI compatibility if on-prem, and kms for keys.
01:27 - Samir Patel: right, our main question: for private customer deployments — they want us to deploy on their VPC or on-prem — what artifacts do you need from infra to test? images, drivers, stuff like that?
01:40 - Owen Brooks: yes, exact. Ideally OS+driver matrix, CUDA/cuDNN versions if using nvidia, preferred container runtime (docker or containerd), and whether customers expect traffic egress to Redwood control plane — some want fully air-gapped.
01:58 - Priya Menon: got it, and SOC2 / audit evidence? Customers often require shep, um, map to SOC2 type II and detailed audit logs.
02:10 - Maya Chen: we can share SOC2 docs and our security whitepaper; for private deployments we support integrating customer KMS/HSM and SAML SSO, and we keep an activity/audit log that meets most enterprise needs. We'll note any gaps for air-gapped installs.
02:25 - Evan Cole: cool. Commercially, NovaForge usually prefers a reseller margin + optional managed service. Curious how Redwood handles reseller pricing and if there's a referral vs reseller contract.
02:38 - Jules Navarro: we have standard reseller addenda and a partner program; margins vary by committed volume, and there's an option for a managed-services referral fee. I can pull samples after the call.
02:50 - Priya Menon: technical detail: our customers often need low p99 latency for chat use-cases, also want cost visibility. How do you handle routing between hosted models and dedicated pools to manage cost/latency?
03:05 - Owen Brooks: short answer: smart routing policies. You can route by latency SLOs, cost tiers, or region. If a dedicated pool can't handle a request, our runtime can failover to a compatible quantized variant in another pool — there's a degradation policy. Also, caching helps with prefix-heavy traffic to reduce tokens.
03:23 - Samir Patel: when you say quantized variant, are we talking int8 INT4 kernels, is that automatic?
03:30 - Owen Brooks: it's configurable; we recommend profiles per workload. Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization levels — but we also do runtime-level kernel selection to handle int8/4 paths where the model supports it.
03:40 - Lina Rodriguez: can we surface that in a pricing model? like show the cost delta for quantized vs baseline?
03:45 - Maya Chen: yes, cost transparency is part of Redwood Console — token-level breakdowns and estimates per config. We can include cost comparisons in the pilot perf spreadsheet.
04:02 - Evan Cole: pilot framing — NovaForge proposes a 6-week pilot with one anchor customer: deploy private on their VPC, run an NLU/chat baseline, measure throughput and p99 latency, and then decide go-to-market packaging. That sound reasonable?
04:17 - Maya Chen: sounds perfect. For scope we usually ask for infra access to run a small cluster + permission to run synthetic workloads. Also, we provide a benchmark runbook.
04:28 - Owen Brooks: yes, and we like to capture model, sequence length distribution, expected concurrency, and token counts. That drives batching and kernel tuning.
04:40 - Samir Patel: we can share a baseline with the customer's approved GPU images — FYI they prefer Tesla A10 for now and a specific CUDA stack.
04:50 - Owen Brooks: A10 is fine; we'll test driver compatibility. If there's a mismatch we'll propose either a different container image or a small shim.
05:00 - Priya Menon: security again — how do you handle logs — where are they stored and for how long? retention?
05:08 - Maya Chen: log retention is configurable; for hosted we store logs in Red-cloud with configurable retention windows tied to the plan. For private deployments we can ship logs to customer S3 or on-prem SIEM, and we integrate with customer KMS so logs can be encrypted at rest with their keys.
05:20 - Evan Cole: ok, good. Are there any customers you've done similar pilots with in telco/regulated space?
05:30 - Maya Chen: yes, a handful — we ran a private pilot with a payments company last quarter and helped them roll out a dedicated pool with strict KMS and RBAC; happy to share a redacted case study.
05:40 - Priya Menon: excellent. On integration effort, how much time do you estimate from kickoff to producing a perf baseline?
05:47 - Owen Brooks: usually 2-3 weeks for initial compatibility and benching, then 3 additional weeks for tuning and final reporting in our typical 5-6 week pilot. This lines up with your 6-week ask.
05:58 - Samir Patel: network — do you need peering or a transit VPN? Some customers won't accept peering.
:06:04 - Owen Brooks: we support multiple patterns: VPC peering, VPN tunnels, and in some cases air-gapped on-prem packages where we hand over runtime bits. We'll need network bandwidth numbers though to estimate throughput.
06:20 - Evan Cole: for commercial model, can NovaForge resell Redwood credits or do you require customer contracts direct?
06:28 - Jules Navarro: both are possible; reseller channel can bill via NovaForge with a margin, or customers can contract direct while NovaForge manages deployment. We'll outline options in the partner packet.
06:40 - Priya Menon: ok, one technical ask: can Redwood runtime run on our managed kubernetes stacks (EKS, GKE) or do you need VM images?
06:50 - Owen Brooks: yes, we have Kubernetes deployment manifests for EKS/GKE and also AMI/VM-based installers for bare-metal. For GPU drivers, we usually recommend a node image with the correct nvidia runtime; for containerized installs we provide Helm charts.
07:05 - Lina Rodriguez: what's the visibility into model versioning and rollouts? our PMs want to pin models for certain customers.
07:12 - Maya Chen: Redwood supports model pinning and rollout policies: canary, A/B, and automatic fallback. Pinning prevents auto-upgrades and you can route specific routes to pinned versions.
07:24 - Evan Cole: any gotchas on telemetry? some customers are strict on PII and we need to scrub logs.
07:30 - Owen Brooks: we support configurable redaction and can opt to not log request bodies; we also offer field-level redaction in console.
07:40 - Priya Menon: excellent. Pricing uncertainty is common; do you have typical pilot discounts?
07:47 - Jules Navarro: yes pilots often run at discounted pilot rates, and we'll propose a committed minimum if they convert. We'll map margins for NovaForge in the SOW.
07:58 - Samir Patel: on the perf side, what's a realistic p99 for a 3B-ish model on A10?
08:04 - Owen Brooks: depends on sequence length and batching. Roughly ballpark, 3B quantized with small seq lengths could do under 200ms p99 in a tuned dedicated pool; hosted multi-tenant is higher. We'll put numbers in the perf spreadsheet.
08:20 - Evan Cole: good. Can you do an initial smoke test with our infra team before the pilot proper? say a single node compatibility test?
08:30 - Maya Chen: yes that's standard — Owen will run the node test with Samir and share the checklist.

12:00 - [speaker swap/misaligned] Speaker 2: um, a question about fallback; if dedicated is saturated, is it transparent to the customer or do they see errors?
12:15 - Owen Brooks: it's transparent if you configure graceful fallback; requests can be routed to a lower-cost or slightly lower-quality variant. You can also set hard SLOs to fail fast instead.
12:32 - Priya Menon: for our internal ops, we need traceability per token for billing — can you export token-level billing?
12:40 - Maya Chen: yep token-level cost export is available; Redwood Console has per-route token and cost breakdowns, and we can push CSVs to your billing pipeline.

18:40 - Samir Patel: curious about KV cache — does that work across model variants? if we roll out updated models do we invalidate cache?
18:52 - Owen Brooks: KV caches are per-model version by default; we have options to namespace caches and to provide warmup strategies to avoid cold-start regressions when changing models.
19:05 - Evan Cole: latency/cost tradeoffs matter to our SMB customers — can we surface recommendations automatically?
19:12 - Maya Chen: Redwood Optimize suggests batching sizes and quantization profiles based on observed workload and cost targets; we can expose suggested configs to NovaForge's managed console.

25:30 - Priya Menon: legal — standard data residency requirements: logs must stay in EU for EU customers. How do you manage multi-region private deployments?
25:40 - Maya Chen: we can pin region and deploy private control planes in-region; for hosted we also offer region-restricted endpoints and data residency add-ons. For private deployments this is straightforward because the control plane can be customer-managed.
25:55 - Evan Cole: good. For the pilot SOW can we include a clause for a follow-up joint GTM workshop?
26:02 - Jules Navarro: yes we'll add a 1-day GTM workshop in week 6 as part of the pilot deliverables.

32:00 - Owen Brooks: quick note on observability: we provide traces and per-token latency heatmaps; you can integrate with Datadog, Splunk, or push to S3. Traces have a sampling rate but we can increase for pilots.
32:15 - Lina Rodriguez: do you expose individual API keys for NovaForge-managed customers?
32:22 - Maya Chen: you can create sub-accounts and per-customer tokens, with RBAC and quota controls.

40:00 - Evan Cole: sounds like good alignment. One potential blocker: some of our customers require HSM integration for signing — do you have HSM/KMS plug-ins?
40:12 - Owen Brooks: yes we integrate with major KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and can talk to external HSM via standardized interfaces; for on-prem HSMs we have a connector pattern — may need some engineering time.
40:30 - Priya Menon: timeline and resourcing — how will Redwood support the pilot? who will be our SE contact?
40:38 - Maya Chen: Owen will be the primary SE, myself for commercial, jules for contracts. We'll provide a single stanza in the SOW for support hours and an escalation path.

48:30 - Samir Patel: for benchmarking, what telemetry should we capture? CPU/GPU utilization, token throughput, batch sizes, p50/p95/p99, memory usage?
48:40 - Owen Brooks: exactly those, plus kernel exec timings and queue wait times. We'll provide a spreadsheet template.
48:52 - Priya Menon: can you simulate realistic traffic? we have burst windows that are important to simulate.
48:58 - Owen Brooks: yes, we can run synthetic workloads that mimic bursty traffic and show how autoscaling and batching affect latency/cost.

55:00 - Maya Chen: ok recap — agreed 6-week pilot, anchor customer private VPC onramp, deliverables: compatibility test, perf benchmark, final report, and a GTM workshop. Action items we listed.
55:20 - Evan Cole: next practical step — samir will send the customer's infra spec and an approved GPU image.
55:28 - Samir Patel: will do today.
55:32 - Jules Navarro: we'll draft the SOW and pilot pricing and send by 9/16.
55:39 - Maya Chen: we'll also attach SOC2 and security docs and the perf runbook.
55:44 - Priya Menon: good — schedule the infra deep-dive next week.
55:48 - Maya Chen: noted — i'll send calendar invite, thanks everyone.
61:45 - Meeting end: wrap up and polite goodbyes, recording stopped.
